units.title: The compensated finite-grid quadratic-variation error has an exact L² norm
units.statement: Let B be a real pre-Brownian process and t₀≤⋯≤tₙ a deterministic grid. If Q is the sum over cells of the squared Brownian increment minus the cell length, then E[Q²] is exactly twice the sum of the squared cell lengths.
assumptions: B satisfies Samplinglib's real pre-Brownian contract under the measure μ.
The deterministic grid has n cells and is monotone in nonnegative real time.
No strict time inequalities, positive horizon, filtration usual conditions, or pathwise boundedness are required.

steps.title: Center one squared increment
steps.text: The Gaussian second and fourth moments give mean zero and second moment 2Δt² for each squared increment after subtracting its time length.

steps.title: Use independence across grid cells
steps.text: Independent Brownian increments remain independent after applying the measurable centered-square map, so distinct centered summands are orthogonal in L².
steps.lean: Use iIndepFun_centeredSquaredIncrement and the finite-sum variance theorem.

steps.title: Add the cell variances
steps.text: Because every summand is square-integrable and centered, the variance of their finite sum is the sum of their variances. Substituting the one-cell identity produces the exact factor 2.
steps.lean: Apply ProbabilityTheory.IndepFun.variance_sum, rewrite variance by the zero mean, and simplify the finite sum.

units.lean_statement: The theorem quantifies over every finite monotone NNReal-time grid and keeps the IsPreBrownianReal process assumption explicit.
units.lean_proof: The proof packages the Gaussian fourth-moment calculation into a one-cell variance, transports independence through the centered-square map, and invokes finite-sum variance additivity.
units.boundary: This theorem is the finite-grid identity only. Its scalar dyadic Tendsto consumer is formalized separately; bounded predictable weights, vector cross-variation, Taylor localization, stochastic integration, and a complete Ito formula remain separate obligations.
